answer: Identity is made expensive: each agent must post a slashable stake locked to one node that answers a rotating liveness challenge. That stake is the anchor, since a puppet caught double-signing loses its escrow, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand at-risk deposits instead of free keys. Voting weight follows stake, not headcount, so a fresh wharf of new accounts sways nothing until real capital backs it. Only after a lockup and review may an identity forge attestations, adding slow onboarding and hosting cost per puppet.
